messages:
Samir: Hey folks — noticed two open PRs that disagree on parse fallback heuristics for tool-calling examples. TL;DR: one suggests always returning an envelope with `tool_name`+`raw_response`, the other prefers a compact JSON when possible. Which direction do we want for the docs?
Maria Chen: leaning compact for the examples — less noise for readers. but we need a clear migration note for existing SDK users.
Jake L: Compact is nicer in the tutorial, but we should show the envelope pattern in an advanced section and in the compatibility guide. People hit prod regressions when they expect the envelope.
Olivia P: Agree with Jake. Suggestion: tutorial + simple SDK snippet that returns compact, and a separate "interop" section showing `envelope` + parse fallback. That way examples map to common patterns.
Samir: Good call. Can we standardize the fallback pseudo-code? proprosal: `if parse_success: return parsed_obj else: return {"tool_name": t, "raw": raw}`. Short and explicit.
Maria Chen: That pseudo-code looks good. Also we should add a small code example for the Python SDK showing how to handle both shapes. I can sketch it.
Jake L: If Maria can do the Python one, I'll add a TS/Node snippet. Keep both under a single cross-language section so links are easy to maintain.
Olivia P: Also: link fixes — the tutorial currently links to the old "invoke" page that was archived. I'll open a tiny PR to update to the new "function-calling" guide.
docs-bot: Reminder: docs PR #4821 is in review and mentions `compact-response` flag.
Samir: Ok owners: Maria -> Python snippet + migration note; Jake -> TS snippet + update samples index; Olivia -> link fixes; I'll write the parse-fallback paragraph and add the envelope example. Can we target EOD tomorrow for a thin PR each?
Maria Chen: EOD tomorrow works for me. I'll also add a unit test snippet showing `assert parse(e) or fallback(e)`.
Jake L: same. Quick Q: should the examples show `raw_response` as a string or as nested JSON? I vote string to avoid assumptions.
Olivia P: string makes sense. If someone needs structured raw, they can `json.loads`. Add that as a note.
Samir: Nice. Also add a tiny example of a streaming response edge-case (interrupted JSON) in the fallback section — real customers hit this. Example: ```json
{"status": "partial", "data": "{\"value\": 1"}
```
Maria Chen: adding that to my snippet. I'll annotate it with `# truncated -> fallback to envelope`.
Jake L: I'll update the SDK examples index doc to point to both snippets and the migration guide. Will ping reviewers after my PR.
Olivia P: PR checklist: update internal anchors + redirect for archived invoke page + run search-and-replace for `compact_response` -> `compact_mode` (we changed the flag last week).
Samir: Good catch on the flag rename. Make sure the snippet code uses the canonical API (v2) and not the legacy examples.
Maria Chen: noted. One last thing — should we include a tiny eval snippet to measure parse-failure rate? Could be useful in the migration note.
Jake L: yes, add a one-liner metric: `parse_fail_rate = failed_parses / total_calls`. Put it under "how to monitor".
Olivia P: I'll queue the linkfix PR now. tagging @docs-owners for review. :thumbsup:
Samir: Perfect. After PRs land I'll assemble a unified follow-up doc for the release notes. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
